nodes.content: Design live firmware updates for an embedded controller that preserve real-time deadlines and actuator consistency across state-schema changes.
requirements: Maintain 1 ms control deadlines throughout uninterrupted updates, without duplicated or skipped actuator commands.
Reject incompatible state migrations atomically; recover a compatible firmware-state pair after any update-time reset.

nodes.content: Keep the 1-ms scheduler and actuator driver resident; validate shadow migrations, atomically switch A/B firmware-state pairs, and sequence-fence commands.
How can the resident scheduler switch firmware-state pairs on a tick boundary without replaying or skipping an actuator sequence?
A tick-boundary pointer swap and resident monotonic command counter keep dispatch below 1 ms with zero duplicates or gaps.
Profile 10,000 tick-boundary swaps under peak load; verify sub-1-ms dispatch and contiguous resident-issued actuator sequence IDs.
Run SwapStress-10k under peak load, recording dispatch latency and resident actuator sequence IDs across 10,000 tick-boundary swaps.
SwapStress-10k recorded 0.82-ms worst-case dispatch latency and zero duplicate or missing actuator sequence IDs across 10,000 swaps.
Select tick-boundary swaps and resident command sequencing for cutover, based on SwapStress-10k's 0.82-ms maximum and gap-free actuator trace.
SwapStress-10k report contains per-tick latency histograms and actuator sequence traces for 10,000 peak-load firmware swaps.
Audit SwapStress-10k report traces for boundary-specific deadline overruns and noncontiguous command IDs, including ticks immediately after each swap.
Audit found seven post-swap actuator latch overruns (maximum 1.08 ms), causing repeated outputs despite contiguous issued command IDs.
Prewarm candidate code and state, prioritize the latch interrupt over cutover, and swap after acknowledgment; each 1-ms tick latches once.
Replay SwapStress-10k report workloads with prewarming and acknowledgment-gated cutover; measure physical latch intervals and deadline misses across 10,000 swaps.
Revised SwapStress-10k measured 0.94-ms maximum latch interval, zero missed deadlines, and 10,000 consecutive acknowledged actuator commands.
Validate shadow migrations before atomically committing a versioned firmware-state pair; after reset, boot the last committed compatible pair.
Test shadow-migration rejection, inject resets at dual-slot commit boundaries, then verify compatible recovery and gap-free 1-ms actuator ticks.
Using SwapStress-10k report's peak-load traces, inject 40 incompatible migrations; verify the active firmware-state pair remains unchanged while actuator latches continue.
MigrationReject-40 log records schema-validation verdicts, active pair identifiers, and physical actuator latch timestamps for 40 incompatible migrations.
Audit MigrationReject-40 for rejection before commit, unchanged firmware-state IDs, and exactly one physical latch per 1-ms tick.
MigrationReject-40 audit found 40/40 rejected before commit, unchanged active pair IDs, and zero missing or duplicate latches.
Adopt prewarmed, acknowledgment-gated cutover with precommit schema rejection: revised swaps met 1-ms deadlines, and MigrationReject-40 preserved active pairs.
How does boot identify a compatible firmware-state pair when reset interrupts the versioned commit record?
Dual CRC-protected records and immutable A/B manifests let boot select the newest fully committed, schema-compatible pair after reset.
Run BootCut-512 with byte-boundary resets across both commit records; check boot selects the newest CRC-valid, schema-compatible firmware-state pair.
BootCut-512 selected the newest fully committed, CRC-valid, schema-compatible pair in all 512 resets; zero mixed pairs booted.
Use tick-stamped copy-on-write snapshots and 50-µs background migration slices, replaying intervening state deltas before cutover.
How can delta replay reach a consistent tick boundary while control ticks keep modifying the snapshot?
Replay SwapStress-10k writes with tick-sealed delta logs and 50-µs slices; verify backlog clearance and cutover-state equality.
SwapStress-10k replay produced 72 µs/tick of delta work; 50-µs slices accrued 220 ms backlog across 10,000 ticks.
Reject fixed 50-µs delta replay: peak-load writes generate 72 µs/tick, preventing convergence before cutover.
Coalescing repeated field writes reduces replay work below 50 µs/tick, allowing sealed-tick backlog to drain before cutover.
Implement tick-sealed, field-keyed coalescing; replay peak-load traces, compare candidate state at cutover, and profile latch intervals.
Run CoalesceReplay-10k on peak-load traces, measuring per-tick replay cost, sealed-log backlog, candidate-state equality, and actuator latch timing.
CoalesceReplay-10k cut replay from 72 to 31 µs/tick; backlog drained, state matched, and latches stayed below 1 ms.
Use CoalesceReplay-10k’s measured 31-µs/tick cost to set a 40-µs replay budget; test burst-write backlog, state equality, and latch timing.
BurstReplay-40 report records 40-µs replay-budget backlog, candidate-state comparisons, and physical latch intervals under burst-write traces.
Add typed migration contracts for actuator-calibration bounds and pending-command ownership, checked against shadow state before atomic cutover.
Typed migration contracts will reject invalid calibration and ambiguous command ownership before commit without missing 1-ms latch deadlines.
Run ContractFault-200 with out-of-range calibration and duplicate command owners; inspect commit records and physical latch intervals under peak load.
ContractFault-200 rejected all 200 invalid states, but synchronous checks pushed three physical latch intervals to 1.06 ms.
How can contract checks run off the control path while guaranteeing validation covers the exact shadow state committed?
Validate immutable shadow generations asynchronously; commit only if the validated generation still matches the shadow at cutover.
Replay BurstReplay-40 traces while mutating shadow generations during asynchronous validation; inspect generation-matched commits, invalid-state rejections, and latch intervals.
BurstReplay-40: 40 stale generations rejected; coalesced replay drained backlog, commits matched validated state, and latch intervals peaked at 0.96 ms.
Integrate generation-locked validation with A/B commits; test peak-load latch continuity and byte-boundary reset recovery to compatible pairs.
Integrate generation-locked validation with A/B commit records; run IntegratedCut-512 with byte-boundary resets and peak-load latch logging.
IntegratedCut-512 dossier extends BurstReplay-40 with generation-locked commit logs, 512 reset recovery traces, compatibility verdicts, and physical latch timestamps.
Core 0 dispatches tick-indexed actuator commands; core 1 migrates firmware, enabling cutover only with validated pairs and ready commands.
How can core 0 consume core 1’s prepared command without stale-cache reads or delaying the 1-ms latch?
Implement uncached tick-tagged mailboxes with release/acquire publication; retain old firmware until ready, then benchmark core-0 latch latency.
Replay IntegratedCut-512 traces on dual cores with uncached tick-tagged mailboxes; measure backlog, state equality, stale reads, latch intervals, recovery.
Dual-core replay: 31 µs/tick coalesced deltas drained backlog; candidate state matched, zero stale reads, 0.96-ms peak latch, 512/512 compatible recoveries.
Adopt dual-core coalesced replay with generation-locked validation, replacing uncoalesced fixed-slice replay; backlog drained and latches peaked at 0.96 ms.
Implement dual-core coalesced replay with generation-locked A/B cutover; regress against IntegratedCut-512 reset, latch, and compatibility traces.
Controller Update v1.0 implements dual-core coalesced migration, generation-locked A/B commits, tick-tagged actuator mailboxes, and IntegratedCut-512 regression tests.
Run MailboxDMA-100k on Controller Update v1.0 under saturated DMA; measure physical latch intervals, mailbox freshness, and command continuity.
MailboxDMA-100k found 11 stale mailbox tags under saturated DMA; physical latch intervals peaked at 1.04 ms despite contiguous IDs.
Block v1.0 deployment after DMA deadline misses; retain precommit migration rejection and CRC-validated A/B boot recovery.
